item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President directs executive-branch procedures for acquiring and using federal space, prescribing priorities and factors for later administrative consideration rather than presently changing legal rights or dictating a specific legal outcome.","evidence":"Procedures for meeting space needs in urban areas shall give serious consideration to the impact a site selection will have"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The provision prescribes a management consideration for later federal site-selection and space-assignment decisions; it does not itself select a site or assign space.","evidence":"Site selection and space assignments shall take into account the management needs for consolidation of agencies or activities"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Administrator must develop programs, issue implementation standards, manage federal space, conduct surveys, and submit plans, but the segment does not dictate a specified legally consequential result.","evidence":"The Administrator of General Services shall develop programs to implement the policies of this Order"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The segment assigns internal information-sharing, consultation, coordination, notice, and impact-assessment responsibilities governing how the Administrator later makes discretionary facilities decisions.","evidence":"Coordinate proposed programs and plans for facilities and space with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget."},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"Executive-agency heads are directed to cooperate in implementation and manage their use of government space economically, an internal administrative mandate.","evidence":"The heads of Executive agencies shall cooperate with the Administrator in implementing the policies of this Order"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The segment imposes internal notice and compliance duties and revokes an earlier executive order; under the codebook, these are executive housekeeping and administrative-governance measures rather than substantive self-executing legal consequences.","evidence":"Executive Order No. 11512 of February 27, 1970, is revoked."}]}
